title: The sodium/iodide symporter (NIS): molecular physiology and preclinical and clinical applications
authors: Ravera S, Reyna-Neyra A, Ferrandino G, Amzel LM, Carrasco N
funder: National Institutes of Health grants DK-41544 (to N. Carrasco) and GM-114250 (to N. Carrasco and L.M. Amzel).
authorConflicts: The authors are not aware of any affiliations, memberships, funding or financial holdings that might be perceived as affecting the objectivity of the review.
result: Review. NIS (SLC5A5) transports iodide into the thyroid electrogenically with a 2 Na+ : 1 I- stoichiometry, driven by the Na+ gradient generated by the Na+/K+-ATPase. Oxidised iodine is incorporated into thyroglobulin, the precursor of T3 and T4. A woman's iodide requirement rises from 150 to 250 µg/day in pregnancy and lactation.
